description: Our interests include healthcare, AI, coding, robotics, clean energy, climate change, law, and business. We are particularly interested in applying AI to improve healthcare and medical research. We also enjoy coding (PCEP and PCAP certified) and robotics, including VEX Robotics. Additionally, we are curious about clean energy solutions to climate change and how law and business can address real-world challenges. We are not looking for members.
summary:
AstraCare is a platform designed to support astronauts’ mental and physical wellbeing throughout space missions. Spaceflight brings challenges beyond physical health, including isolation, confinement, and increase psychological pressures.

At its core, AstraCare gives astronauts a space to express themselves freely. Through daily check-ins, journaling, and voice recordings, astronauts can share their thoughts, emotions, and experiences in their own words. Voice reflections allow them to speak naturally rather than structure their feelings into forms, helping capture aspects of their wellbeing that numbers alone cannot reveal.

AstraCare combines these reflections with personalized health baselines and physiological data, including sleep, heart rate, and activity, to identify changes over time. Its AI works quietly in the background rather than providing unsolicited feedback. If explicit safety concerns, such as references to suicide, are detected, an alert is flagged for a healthcare professional.

Designed primarily for offline use, AstraCare stores information locally and synchronizes records and alerts when connectivity becomes available, accounting for communication delays between Mars and Earth.

Through its AI-powered Glance Report and dedicated healthcare professional workspace, AstraCare supports continuous monitoring and human oversight. Ultimately, we want astronauts to feel heard, understood, and supported, even millions of kilometres from home.
details:
When astronauts travel beyond Earth, healthcare cannot depend on information being constantly transmitted back home. During missions to Mars, communication delays can make immediate assistance impossible. This creates a need for a system that can independently collect, understand, and monitor an astronaut’s wellbeing while keeping healthcare professionals involved whenever communication becomes available. This is the problem AstraCare is designed to address.

AstraCare collects information through daily check-ins, written journal entries, and voice reflections. Check-ins use a 1–5 rating system across sleep, stress, energy, mood, concentration, connection, and isolation. Voice recordings are transcribed directly on the device using Whisper Tiny, a speech-to-text AI model, allowing spoken experiences to be analyzed alongside written entries without sending recordings to an online AI service.

Its main feature is personalization. Instead of comparing astronauts against general population averages, AstraCare creates an individual baseline over 21 days, requiring at least 14 completed check-ins. It establishes a starting point across six wellbeing dimensions, adjusting scores so higher values consistently represent better wellbeing. As new information is collected, the baseline can gradually update using an 80:20 weighted average, with movement limited to 0.3 points. To maintain consistency, the baseline will be excluded from concerning days to it doesn't mistake it as a normal day and create an inaccurate mental health indicator. This is not saying that the AI will not consider concerning days and give feedback, we are just stating how it will maintain an accurate baseline.

The system then compares recent check-ins with personal baselines, examining weekly averages, longer-term changes, and connections between different dimensions. It also identifies recurring topics in written and spoken reflections, such as fatigue, workload, missing home, and difficulties with crew members. This allows numerical changes to be understood alongside the experiences behind them.

All AI processing happens locally. Alongside Whisper Tiny, AstraCare uses a compressed Llama 3.1 1B Instruct model, running directly on the device using GPU processing. A separate rules-based system handles numerical analysis and safety screening, checking for explicit high-risk language, including references to suicide. Detected concerns create alerts for healthcare professionals, which are stored locally until communication becomes available.

The application is built around two distinct views: an astronaut workspace and a healthcare professional workspace. Both are already implemented and connected through a shared account and workspace system. Users create an account or sign in, then choose their role by either creating a workspace as a healthcare professional or joining an existing workspace using an invitation code as an astronaut. Healthcare professionals can create and manage workspaces, invite astronauts and other professionals, and review the information shared with them. Astronauts have their own dashboard for daily check-ins, reflections, physiological monitoring, and personal insights. Each view has its own tools and access permissions, and an account with both memberships can switch between the two views.

The entire design is built around operating without a continuous connection to Earth. Journal entries, recordings, transcripts, personal baselines, and AI analysis are stored and processed on the device. The platform also has a sensor interface for heart rate, HRV, sleep, activity, skin temperature, and breathing rate (currently using simulated readings). When a connection becomes available, authorized information, transcripts, and queued alerts can synchronize with the healthcare professional workspace. Original voice recordings remain on the astronaut’s device.

AstraCare brings together individual health tracking, personal expression, on-device AI, and two connected user experiences to provide a more complete approach to astronaut healthcare. It gives astronauts a system that works independently during a mission while giving healthcare professionals a way to stay informed, connected, and involved in their care.
